provenance.para:
**Provenance.** Every figure is recomputed from `eval_results/data_3_6_flash_v8/`, over **34 analysis cells**: `aligned_setting_{low,medium,high}/<Vendor>/<model>/` for the 10 swept models (18,000 episodes) plus `aligned_setting_high_ocr/<Vendor>/<model>/` (v4-flash) and `open_source_high/<Vendor>/<model>/` (v4-pro, glm-5.2 and kimi-k3) for the 4 open-source models, which were run once at `high` rather than swept (2,400 episodes) — **20,400 episodes in total**, each cell being 60 scenarios × 10 rounds = 600 tasks. `aligned_setting_high_ocr` is a staging directory, not an OCR condition — the runs under it were not preprocessed with OCR, and the name is describing that they were served asset file paths as text (`multimodal_input_mode=path`), which is stated as a run condition below in its own right. The run subdirectory is `r01/` throughout, with one exception — 3.7-flash is read from `r02`, for the reason given under run conditions below.

The corpus is **not** a clean cross-product, so do not multiply anything by 14 here: only 10 of the 14 models have an effort sweep, which is why §9 covers 10 models and every other section covers 14.

Unless a table says otherwise, figures are at `reasoning_effort=high`, the primary setting: 14 models × 600 tasks = **8,400 episodes** and **120,575 recorded actions**. Regenerate with:

```
python tools/build_behavior_report.py --root $CLASHARNESS_DATA_ROOT --effort high
```

**Not every row here is like-for-like.** v4-pro, v4-flash and glm-5.2 were handed asset file paths as text and never received an image (`multimodal_input_mode=path`); kimi-k3, the open-source model that did receive images, is the control; also, 3.7-flash is reported on `r02`, the higher of its two complete runs, where every other row is a single run (the two differ by 1.7pp, McNemar p=0.27). Full statement: [run conditions](#run-conditions-that-are-not-comparable).

**Not every row here is like-for-like.** v4-pro, v4-flash and glm-5.2 were handed asset file paths as text and never received an image (`multimodal_input_mode=path`); kimi-k3, the open-source model that did receive images, is the control; also, 3.7-flash is reported on `r02`, the higher of its two complete runs, where every other row is a single run (the two differ by 1.7pp, McNemar p=0.27). Full statement: [run conditions](#run-conditions-that-are-not-comparable).
roster.conditions: **Run conditions that are not comparable across the field.** All 14 models ran the same harness build, the same 600 tasks and the same nominal effort; what follows is the residue that did not align. Each line is read off that model's own episode headers and checked against this list on every build. - **3.7-flash** — run selection: reported on r02, the higher of its two complete runs, while every other model is reported on its single r01 — r01 scored 18.67% and r02 20.33% (paired: 38 gained, 28 lost, McNemar p=0.27), so the gap is within run-to-run noise and this row is a best-of-two where the others are single draws. - **v4-pro** — multimodal_input_mode=path (never received an image); reasoning_effort=high, set via chat_template_kwargs (with thinking=true) rather than the API field; harness max_image_edge=1920 rather than the 2576 the other thirty-one cells used, which is inert for a model sent no images. - **v4-flash** — multimodal_input_mode=path (never received an image); reasoning_effort=high, set via chat_template_kwargs (with thinking=true) rather than the API field; harness max_image_edge=1920 rather than the 2576 the other thirty-one cells used, which is inert for a model sent no images. - **kimi-k3** — multimodal_input_mode=both; reasoning_effort medium requested, high served. - **glm-5.2** — multimodal_input_mode=path (never received an image); reasoning_effort=high, set via chat_template_kwargs rather than the API field; served FP8-quantized (zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8); harness max_image_edge=1920 rather than the 2576 the other thirty-one cells used, which is inert for a model sent no images. These are conditions, not excuses, and this report does not assert that any of them caused the scores they sit beside. The one that looks most damning is measurably not. The corpus’ required grounding check scores whether the needed asset was *opened* — which a file path supports — and on the 343 tasks where all fourteen models have it scored, the three path-mode models rank **1st, 3rd and 6th of fourteen** (glm-5.2 95.3%, v4-flash 93.6%, v4-pro 91.3%). So the ranking is **led** by one of them, and its floor — sonnet-5 at 77.8%, 17.5 points below — is a model that did receive images. The two input modes also do not separate into two score populations: the path-mode band — **8.5% to 19.8%** pass — lies inside the **3.0%–25.2%** the image-receiving models span, and the two rows at its ends (v4-flash and v4-pro, DeepSeek’s own two entries) ran under identical conditions yet finish **11.3 points** apart. So the path rows are best read as measurements of those models; this corpus does not isolate an effect of the mode itself. Separately, the 4 open-source models were run **once**, at `high`, so they appear in every main table but not in the effort chapter (§9).
